items.content: <article>Coreboot downstream Libreboot last month enacted an AI policy to forbid contributions made using AI/LLMs. Surprisingly, already, that anti-AI policy has been dropped with AI-based submissions now being permitted...</article>

items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Werner Koch announced a late Friday afternoon "critical security bug" affecting GnuPG's GPGME library - GnuPG Made Easy. Unfortunately this in turn affects GPGME users like most email clients, most XMPP clients, Flatpak, Samba, and other software...</article>

items.content: <article>A change set to land for the upcoming Linux 7.5 kernel cycle expands the mmap range size for GEM/TTM buffer objects in the kernel graphics drivers from 1TB to now up to 8TB...</article>

items.title: AMD Contributes Integration For Content-Adaptive / Adaptive Backlight Modulation To GNOME
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Merged today to GNOME's Mutter compositor is support for the Adaptive Backlight Modulation (ABM) DRM/KMS connector property and a "content-adaptive" API. This GNOME desktop improvement was contributed by AMD as part of modern AMD Ryzen AI laptops supporting Adaptive Backlight Modulation...</article>

items.title: System76 Thelio Prime: A Petite But Performant AMD-Powered Linux PC
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>After teasing the new System76 Thelio Prime last month, this week officially launched their redesigned Thelio Prime mini desktop PC. This AMD Ryzen 9000 series powered creation is quite small with an internal volume of just 9.78 liters but quite capable with up to the Ryzen 9 9900X being supported, AMD or NVIDIA discrete graphics options, up to 96GB of RAM, and up to 16TB of NVMe storage. I have been testing out the new Thelio Prime for the past few days so far and it's been stacking up as well as one of their best compact PCs yet.</article>

items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>A patch that is queued up ahead of the Linux 7.5 merge window allows for optionally disabling /proc/kcore access at boot time. This can allow for better system security though will remain enabled by default for kernel builds with the typical CONFIG_PROC_KCORE option...</article>

items.title: LLVM Effectively Completes Its Relicensing After Nearly A Decade Of Work
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Back around 2017 an effort began to work on re-licensing all of the LLVM code under the Apache 2.0 license with exceptions, moving away from their prior 3-clause BSD-like "LLVM license". Prior updates on the topic included LLVM Developers Are Still Working On Their Massive Relicensing Effort (2018) and then LLVM Is Still Working On Relicensing, Needs Help Locating Some Past Contributors (2021)... Now finally as we approach the end of 2026, this re-licensing effort has been deemed effectively complete...</article>

items.title: AI-Powered Sashiko Introduces Experimental Patch Series Design Assessment
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>When it comes to leveraging AI for Linux kernel development, one of the most widely-used solutions at the moment is Sashiko that has evolved nicely over the past year for agentic AI code review. This AI-driven screening of generated code posted to the Linux kernel mailing list constantly identifies bugs and other code defects in a quick and straight-forward manner. With being developed and maintained by Google engineers, it uses Gemini by default but is LLM-agnostic overall. Released on Tuesday was Sashiko v0.9.4 as the next step forward for this Linux kernel helper...</article>

items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>The PC Engines APU2 single board computer debuted all the way back in 2015 with the AMD Jaguar-powered GX-412TC quad-core SoC and 2~4GB of DDR3 memory. While PC Engines discontinued the APU2 SBC several years ago, these boards have been quite popular for networking/firewall applications and other similar low-power, networking-oriented setups. If you still happen to be using PC Engines APU2 hardware, 3mdeb today released updated system firmware for this decade old SBC...</article>
